subject: Intermittent long-tail completions impacting checkout — immediate action plan
messages:
From: Cassandra Li <cassandra@fintrove.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Fintrove SRE <sre@fintrove.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Mar 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent slow completions in checkout (p95->p99 gap)

Aditya —

We saw a repeating pattern this morning where 1–2% of checkout LLM completions take 8–12s (our target is <1.5s). This shows up as order confirmation timeouts and page hangs for web checkout. We captured two sample request IDs in the attachment and a short heap snapshot from our side.

Can Redwood confirm root cause and escalation path? We had to flip to a mitigation (reduced concurrency) to avoid timeouts, but that’s not sustainable. This started after your last model rollout a week ago.

-Jordan (on behalf of Cassandra)
Cassandra Li
Head of Platform, Fintrove

Cassandra — thanks for the heads up and the samples. I’m escalating to our on-call infra and runtime team now. Initial questions:

- Can you confirm if the problematic requests include any unusually long prompts or tool calls?
- Are the slow completions correlated with specific models or routes (chat vs. generation)?

What I’m doing now: looping Hannah (runtime on-call) and Vivek (capacity/placement). Lauren, any immediate context on the model variant we rolled last week?

We’ll triage and come back within 90 min with initial findings and a mitigation plan.

—Aditya

From: hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: aditya.rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, lauren.bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, vivek.kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Mar 2029 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent slow completions in checkout (p95->p99 gap)

Aditya — quick triage notes (internal):

1) Telemetry: we see correlated spikes on the request queue depth and KV-cache miss rate for the Fintrove tenant across a small subset of instances (instance group rg-12). The p99 aligns with enforcement of the concurrency cap on those boxes; when cap is hit requests queue and service time inflates.

2) Root cause hypothesis: the recent model variant (v3-compact-q4) introduced slightly larger per-request memory working set (longer attention + extra tool metadata). On rg-12 the compiled kernels push memory pressure to the soft limit, and our eviction policy stalls ongoing completions while performing GC-like reclaim. That shows as 6–12s outliers.

3) Immediate mitigation I applied: temporarily raised concurrency cap on rg-12 by +30% and enabled aggressive kvprefetch for that tenant. That reduced the p99 in the last 15m on the sampled machines.

4) Engineering next steps: full heap snapshots from affected instances (I pulled two — see attachment), reproduce locally with identical model + sequence length distribution, and add a targeted micro-optimization to the attention kernel.

I’ll follow up with reproduction notes within 4 hours. If we need capacity, Vivek — please advise on short window burst or hot-pool migration.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: heap_snapshot.log (text)]

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: hannah.schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, aditya.rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, lauren.bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Mar 2029 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent slow completions in checkout (p95->p99 gap)

Thanks Hannah — short note on capacity options (internal):

- Hot-pool migration: we can evacuation-migrate Fintrove’s traffic from rg-12 to hot-pool-3 with a <15 min impact window. That buys headroom while kernel fix ships.
- Short-term reserved burst: we can spin 4x temporary slots in us-west and pin Fintrove there for 6 hours; costly but low-risk.
- Longer-term: schedule model-variant profiling on dedicated nodes to avoid co-tenancy memory pressure.

I recommend: 1) migrate traffic to hot-pool-3 now, 2) set model rollout to v3-compact-q3 (previous) for Fintrove as a fallback flag, 3) route engineering to optimize kernel memory allocation. Lauren, I need approvals for a hot-pool migration and a rollback flag for the customer-specific rollout.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Capacity & Orchestration, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Cassandra Li <cassandra@fintrove.com>, Fintrove SRE <sre@fintrove.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, vivek.kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Mar 2029 18:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent slow completions in checkout (p95->p99 gap) — short-term plan and ETA

Cassandra / Fintrove team —

Thanks again for flagging and for the sample traces. Summary and plan:

What we saw
- Small subset (~1.8%) of completions were hitting 6–12s due to queueing on a handful of instances (rg-12) under a new model variant.

Immediate actions completed
- Migrated Fintrove traffic from rg-12 to hot-pool-3 (completed 2029-03-05 11:20 PT) — this removed the immediate queueing and reduced the p99 below 2s for the last 36h.
- Rolled back the Fintrove rollout flag to v3-compact-q3 while we validate kernel fixes.
- Enabled a tenant-scoped concurrency bump and kvprefetch for Fintrove while we confirm fix and mitigation stability.

Next steps and ETA
- Hannah/Runtime to land an attention-kernel memory-reduction patch (in progress). ETA: 48–72 hours for canary + validation.
- Vivek/Capacity to schedule a dedicated profiling run and propose a placement policy change for memory-sensitive variants. ETA: 5 business days.
- I’ll provide a post-mortem within 5 business days with telemetry, reproducer, and recommended rollout guardrails.

Attachments: SLO impact summary and heap snapshots (attached).

If you want an exec sync, I can set up a 30-min call Thursday with our head of runtime and capacity. Otherwise we will continue with the current mitigations and keep you updated.

—Aditya Rao
Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
